title: Jemimah Rodrigues Named Switzerland Tourism's Friendship Ambassador for India
excerpt: The World Cup-winning cricketer follows Neeraj Chopra in the role and will front a four-season campaign aimed at younger Indian travellers, from Interlaken's jetboats to Zurich's e-bikes.
body:
• Switzerland Tourism has named Indian cricketer Jemimah Rodrigues as its Friendship Ambassador for India, announced in Bengaluru in the presence of CEO Martin Nydegger.
  • Rodrigues follows javelin star Neeraj Chopra in the role and will showcase Switzerland across all four seasons, from Interlaken and Jungfraujoch to Zurich.
  • India ranks among Switzerland Tourism's top 10 source markets, and the campaign targets younger travellers seeking personal, experience-led trips beyond the standard summer circuit.
  • Planning a Swiss trip: Indian passport holders need a Schengen visa for short stays — check the rules on Switzerland Tourism's visa page for Indian passport holders before booking.

Switzerland Tourism has appointed Indian cricketer Jemimah Rodrigues as its Friendship Ambassador for India, the organisation announced in Bengaluru in the presence of its chief executive, Martin Nydegger. Rodrigues becomes the second high-profile Indian athlete to hold the role, after two-time Olympic medallist javelin thrower Neeraj Chopra, according to Mint's report of the announcement.

The appointment comes while Rodrigues is out of the Indian team, recuperating from a high-grade right hamstring strain sustained during The Hundred that forced her to miss the Asia Cup and the Asian Games. A member of India's Women's ODI World Cup-winning team in 2025, she remains one of the most recognisable faces of Indian women's cricket.

"Representing India has always been something very special to me, and wherever I travel, I carry a little bit of home with me. What excites me about this association is the chance to discover Switzerland beyond everything we already know and love about it."

— Jemimah Rodrigues, cricketer

What the campaign will show

The campaign film follows Rodrigues through Interlaken and Zurich, presenting two different sides of the country. In Interlaken she took a jetboat ride, tried Swiss chocolate-making and visited Ballenberg, the open-air museum of Swiss heritage. At Jungfraujoch she experienced snow for the first time. In Zurich, she explored the city by running, riding an e-bike and taking an electric boat across Lake Zurich, according to India Outbound's account of the launch. Over the course of the association she will travel in all four seasons, covering well-known highlights alongside lesser-known regions.

Why Switzerland is courting younger Indians

India ranks among Switzerland Tourism's top 10 source markets, and the organisation says the profile of the Indian visitor is changing. "Today's Indian traveller is curious, confident and increasingly looking for experiences that feel personal and authentic. Jemimah brings that spirit naturally," Nydegger said. Christian Schoch, Switzerland Tourism's director for India, said long-haul markets such as India have an important role in strengthening year-round tourism, especially in mountain regions, and tied the campaign to the organisation's "Travel Better" philosophy: encouraging visitors to stay longer, explore further and look beyond the traditional highlights.

The strategy matters because Indian travel to Switzerland has historically concentrated in the April-to-June window. A four-season ambassador programme is aimed at spreading those visits into autumn and winter, when the same destinations are quieter.

What this means for travellers

For Indian and diaspora travellers considering Switzerland outside the summer rush, the practical starting points are unchanged: plan around the seasons you want, and sort the paperwork early. Indian passport holders must hold a visa to visit Switzerland; Switzerland Tourism's visa regulations page for Indian passport holders sets out the Schengen short-stay rules, and its Grand Tour of Switzerland facts page is a useful route-planning reference for a road-based itinerary. Rodrigues's first campaign content, from Interlaken and Zurich, is already out; further seasonal films are expected as the association runs.
